prompt: An order row holds `customer_id = 2`, a date and a total, and no name. Is it personal data?
hint: Identified or identifiable.

choices.text: No, because nobody is named in it
choices.why: No. The law covers identifiable people, not only named ones.

choices.text: Yes; the id joins to a person
choices.why: Right. Identifiable through other data is enough.

choices.text: Only if the total is above a threshold
choices.why: No. The amount does not decide it.

choices.text: Only while the customer is active
choices.why: No. Activity has nothing to do with the definition.

prompt: Match each role in the LGPD to who plays it at Ipê.
hint: One decides, one acts for it, one is the channel.

prompt: Which of these are personal data at Ipê? Choose all that apply.
hint: Related to an identifiable person.

choices.text: The time a delivery arrived at a customer's address
choices.why: Yes. It says when somebody was at home.

choices.text: A customer's choice to accept marketing
choices.why: Yes. A choice a person made is about them.

choices.text: The price of a box of dipirona
choices.why: No. The catalogue says nothing about anybody until somebody buys.

choices.text: The address of one of Ipê's shops
choices.why: No. It is about the company, not a person.

prompt: Which of these is on the LGPD's list of sensitive personal data?
hint: Article 5, II.

choices.text: A bank account number
choices.why: No. It is personal data, and protected, but not on the list.

choices.text: A home address
choices.why: No. Personal, not sensitive in the legal sense.

choices.text: Trade union membership
choices.why: Right. Along with health, religion, politics, ethnicity, sex life, genetics and biometrics.

choices.text: A salary
choices.why: No. Personal, not on the list.

prompt: Can a company add 'purchase history' to the legal list of sensitive data by declaring it so?
hint: The list is closed; what changes is what the data reveals.

choices.text: Yes, in its privacy policy
choices.why: No. A policy cannot extend the law's list.

choices.text: No, though a revealing one is
choices.why: Right. The list is closed, and a history revealing health is health data: what the data reveals decides whether it falls in the list.

choices.text: Yes, by asking the ANPD to register it
choices.why: No. There is no such register.

choices.text: No, and purchase histories are never sensitive
choices.why: No. A pharmacy's are, through health.

prompt: How many customers bought a product in the category `diagnostic`, the pregnancy test?
hint: The last row of the result.

prompt: A marketing team trains a model on Ipê's purchase histories to recommend products. What is the model processing?
hint: What can a recommendation reveal about the buyer?

choices.text: Only catalogue data, since products are not personal
choices.why: No. The histories are people's purchases.

choices.text: Ordinary personal data, since no diagnosis is stored
choices.why: No. A diagnosis can be inferred, which is enough.

choices.text: Health data, including inferences people never shared
choices.why: Right. Article 11 then decides whether there is a basis for it at all.

choices.text: Anonymous data, because models do not store rows
choices.why: No. A model trained on personal data makes personal inferences.

prompt: Why does section 7 classify `sales.order_items.product_id` as sensitive?
hint: Follow the join.

choices.text: Because it is a foreign key
choices.why: No. Plenty of foreign keys are not sensitive.

choices.text: Because the products table is sensitive
choices.why: No. The catalogue alone is class none.

choices.text: Because it is in the schema sales
choices.why: No. The schema does not decide it.

choices.text: What was bought reveals health
choices.why: Right. A pharmacy's order line is health data by what it reveals.

prompt: How many of the customers under eighteen accepted marketing?
hint: Add the two rows.

prompt: Under Brazilian law, a customer aged 16 is…
hint: The Statute of the Child and Adolescent draws the line at 12.

choices.text: a child, so parental consent is the article's rule
choices.why: No. A child is under 12.

choices.text: an adolescent, under the best-interest test
choices.why: Right. Article 14 covers both, with the best interest above all.

choices.text: an adult for data purposes
choices.why: No. Under 18 is a minor.

choices.text: outside the LGPD entirely
choices.why: No. The LGPD has an article for them.

prompt: Ipê's terms say customers must be adults, and the data holds twenty under eighteen. What is the data team's finding?
hint: A rule and the data disagree.

choices.text: The twenty rows are errors to delete
choices.why: No. They are real accounts the controls let in.

choices.text: The terms are wrong and should allow minors
choices.why: No. That is the business's decision, not the data team's.

choices.text: A missing sign-up control
choices.why: Right. A control that should exist at sign-up does not; report it, with the numbers, to the DPO and the business.

choices.text: Nothing; age is not personal data
choices.why: No. Age is personal data, and article 14 makes it matter more.

prompt: Which article of the LGPD requires controllers and processors to keep a record of processing operations?
hint: It is in the chapter on agents of processing.

choices.text: Article 5
choices.why: No. Article 5 is definitions.

choices.text: Article 11
choices.why: No. Article 11 is sensitive data.

choices.text: Article 14
choices.why: No. Article 14 is children and adolescents.

choices.text: Article 37
choices.why: Right. Especially when the basis is legitimate interest.

prompt: How many columns did the first inventory count across Ipê's ten tables?
hint: Add the column counts.

prompt: Why does every row of `gov.column_class` carry a `why`?
hint: What happens to a label nobody can explain?

choices.text: PostgreSQL requires a comment on every row
choices.why: No. It is a column the table defines as NOT NULL by choice.

choices.text: So a class is never undone blindly
choices.why: Right. A classification with no reason is a label somebody will undo.

choices.text: Because the ANPD reads it
choices.why: No. It is for the people who maintain the database.

choices.text: To make the table harder to fill
choices.why: No. Friction is not the aim.

prompt: Put what happened to `coupon_code` in order.
hint: The check found it the day it appeared.

prompt: Where should `unclassified.sql` run to make adding an unclassified column impossible rather than discouraged?
hint: Where schema changes are applied.

choices.text: Once a year, before the audit
choices.why: No. A year of unclassified columns is the problem it should prevent.

choices.text: On the analysts' laptops
choices.why: No. They do not change the schema.

choices.text: Inside the support view
choices.why: No. A view cannot fail a migration.

choices.text: In the migration pipeline
choices.why: Right. Where migrations are applied, failing the run: the same property as the platform's registry test.

prompt: What does the platform's privacy registry do that Ipê's classification table does not yet?
hint: Read the OnErase values.

choices.text: It classifies columns instead of tables
choices.why: No. The registry classifies tables.

choices.text: It decides what erasure does to each table
choices.why: Right. The export and erase paths are built from it.

choices.text: It encrypts each table it lists
choices.why: No. It classifies; encryption is elsewhere.

choices.text: It replaces the database's grants
choices.why: No. Grants are unaffected.

prompt: Match each OnErase value to what erasing a person does to the table's rows.
hint: One keeps them on purpose.

pairs.right: the rows stay and point at nobody
the rows stay, and are meant to

prompt: How many of the 1,500 tickets contained something shaped like a CPF?
hint: The second column.

prompt: Why is `support.tickets.body` classified as sensitive, though the form was designed for delivery complaints?
hint: Who decides what goes into a free-text field?

choices.text: Because tickets are always about health
choices.why: No. Most are about deliveries.

choices.text: Because it is longer than the other columns
choices.why: No. Length is not the test.

choices.text: Whatever anybody typed decides it
choices.why: Right. Its class is the most sensitive thing anybody typed, and 26 tickets named a medicine.

choices.text: Because support agents read it
choices.why: No. Who reads a column does not change what it holds.

prompt: The redacted view replaces CPFs, e-mail addresses and 'I take …'. What does it still let through?
hint: Patterns find shapes, not meanings.

choices.text: Nothing, because every pattern is covered
choices.why: No. No set of patterns covers every way to describe health.

choices.text: Health written in words no pattern knows
choices.why: Right. A count of what patterns catch is a floor, never the whole.

choices.text: The ticket's id
choices.why: No. The id was kept on purpose; it identifies a ticket.

choices.text: Every CPF written without dots
choices.why: No. That is a pattern gap too, but the larger gap is meaning.

prompt: 'The business finds it useful.' Can that support processing sensitive data?
hint: Article 11 has its own, shorter list.

choices.text: Yes, as legitimate interest
choices.why: No. Legitimate interest is not among article 11's bases.

choices.text: Yes, if the DPO agrees
choices.why: No. The DPO cannot create a basis the law does not have.

choices.text: No; article 11 allows only its own bases
choices.why: Right. Specific consent, or a short list of cases such as legal obligation or health protection.

choices.text: Yes, if the data is encrypted
choices.why: No. Encryption is protection, not a legal basis.

prompt: A partner offers to pay Ipê for its customers' purchase histories. Which part of the LGPD speaks to this most directly?
hint: Sharing health data for an economic advantage.

choices.text: Article 37, the record of processing
choices.why: No. The record would describe the sale; it does not forbid it.

choices.text: Article 14, children's data
choices.why: No. Relevant for the twenty adolescents, not the core of it.

choices.text: Article 11, §4
choices.why: Right. It forbids sharing health data for economic advantage outside health services and the person's interest.

choices.text: Article 6, III, necessity
choices.why: No. Necessity applies, but §4 names this case.

prompt: Match each class to the legal basis it needs.
hint: One needs none.

prompt: Ipê asks for a full date of birth to refuse sales to minors. What does the necessity principle suggest?
hint: What does the purpose actually need?

choices.text: Keep the date and encrypt it
choices.why: No. Encryption protects it; it does not ask whether it is needed.

choices.text: Ask whether the customer is an adult, and at most the year
choices.why: Right. The purpose needs adulthood, not the day of birth.

choices.text: Ask for a copy of an identity document instead
choices.why: No. That collects more, not less.

choices.text: Nothing; the date is already collected
choices.why: No. Minimisation applies to what is already held too.

prompt: Article 6, III of the LGPD names the principle of ___: processing limited to the minimum its purposes need.
hint: Minimum needed.

prompt: Why does the lab generate every CPF with a wrong second check digit?
hint: What could a valid one be?

choices.text: To test the validator's speed
choices.why: No. Speed is not the point.

choices.text: Because valid CPFs are hard to generate
choices.why: No. The first check digit is generated right.

choices.text: So none of them is a real person's
choices.why: Right. A number with valid digits belongs to somebody until shown otherwise; one that fails belongs to nobody.

choices.text: Because the LGPD forbids storing valid CPFs
choices.why: No. Ipê stores real CPFs legitimately in real life.

prompt: The check reported '6012 pass the first check digit, 0 pass both'. What does the first number prove?
hint: A check that finds nothing might be broken.

choices.text: That the validator works
choices.why: Right. Without it, 0 valid could mean a broken check.

choices.text: That the CPFs are real
choices.why: No. None passes both digits.

choices.text: That the file is complete
choices.why: No. It counts digits, not rows missing.

choices.text: That the database still holds CPFs
choices.why: No. The check read the generated file because it does not.

prompt: Match each column to its class at Ipê.
hint: What does each reveal?

prompt: A new table `sales.loyalty` adds points per customer. What has to happen before it ships?
hint: The check fails otherwise.

choices.text: Nothing; points are not personal data
choices.why: No. Points per customer are about a person.

choices.text: An entry in the privacy policy, and nothing in the database
choices.why: No. The classification check would fail the migration.

choices.text: A class and a why for each of its columns
choices.why: Right. Deciding what it holds, in the same change.

choices.text: Encryption of every column with OpenBao
choices.why: No. The class decides the handling, not the reverse.
